candidate.answerReason: Expanding the square produces the middle term -10√(y²-25), while the two constant terms cancel.

methods.label: Expand the square
methods.explanation:
For real \(y\), the expression is defined when \(y^2-25\ge0\), or \(|y|\ge5\). Use \((a-b)^2=a^2-2ab+b^2\), keeping the middle term:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left(5-\sqrt{y^2-25}\right)^2
&=25-10\sqrt{y^2-25}+(y^2-25)\\
&=y^2-10\sqrt{y^2-25}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \((\sqrt{y^2-25})^2=y^2-25\) because the radicand is nonnegative. The result is \(\boxed{y^2-10\sqrt{y^2-25}}\), choice E.
methods.levelReason: This is a direct application of the binomial-square identity and the square-root identity on its real domain.
